subject: Sandstone: P0 latency amplification -> AZ2 routing action & exec brief
messages:
From: Elaine Nguyen <elaine.nguyen@sandstone.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Sandstone Ops <ops@sandstone.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: High latency + 500s in us-west-2 (AZ2) — critical for ad delivery

Sergio / Redwood team,

We started seeing a ~10x spike in inference latency and a rise in 500 responses from your API servicing our campaign traffic out of us-west-2 (AZ2) starting ~09:05 PDT. This is a hard P0 for us — live ad auctions are failing and we risk missing the peak window.

App details: model:redwood-alpha-v1 (pinned), traffic ~2.2k QPS, median latency normally ~85ms, currently tail > 2.1s and 5xxs ~4%. We have request IDs if you need them.

Can you confirm mitigation plan and expected ETA to stabilize? If you need us to approve cross-region routing to us-west-1 for a temporary period, please say so — we will authorize. Also please share whether this will incur credits for the outage window.

— Elaine
Elaine Nguyen
Head of Platform, Sandstone Media

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-04T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: RE: High latency + 500s in us-west-2 (AZ2) — immediate actions and exec ask

Team — quick summary and recommended actions (we have pager and metrics linked below; attaching a short diagnostic brief):

What happened: beginning ~09:05 PDT, AZ2 experienced sharp KV-cache miss amplification for the redwood-alpha-v1 prefix workloads from Sandstone. KV cache eviction patterns + a kernel scheduling hiccup caused latency amplification and a small rate of 5xxs when the runtime hit an edge-case memory pressure path.

Customer impact: Sandstone production traffic (high QPS ad routing) — tail latency >2s, 5xx ~4%, immediate revenue impact. Customer willing to accept geo-failover if we authorize.

Immediate mitigation (I recommend we enact now):
- Toggle routing policy for Sandstone prod to prefer us-west-1 (cross-region steer) for 30 minutes, with automatic revert after stabilization.
- Spin up 2x temporary Dedicated capacity in us-west-1 (auto-provisioned) to maintain headroom during failover.
- Enable aggressive prefix caching for Sandstone routes and pin model variant to reduce kernel path variance.
- Notify customer and confirm cutover time 09:35 PDT.

Reqs for approval:
- Exec approval to perform cross-region steer (security/consent provided by customer).
- Approval for temporary Dedicated overprovisioning charge + discretionary incident credit (customer is asking about credits).

Estimated timeline: routing change + cache pinning: 5–7 minutes once approved; Dedicated capacity ~8–12 minutes to be fully ready.

Links: Pager INC-2027-0042, Drive diagnostic (attached), real-time graphs: https://redwood.internal/pager/INC-2027-0042

Attachments: diagnostic-brief.pdf, latency-graphs.png, kvcache-excerpt.txt

Requested next steps: Aditya / Marissa — can you please sign off on cross-region steer and up to 25% credit for the impacted window (we propose 20% initially). Hannah — engineering to stand by to execute at :35. Vanessa — own the customer comm templates.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
